pages.title: Title
pages.summary: Quality and Defensive Investing.

pages.title: Roadmap
pages.summary: Quality definitions and the value link; Novy-Marx profitability; comparing measures; Betting Against Beta; Quality Minus Junk; decomposing Buffett. Running question: do safe, profitable firms earn HIGHER risk-adjusted returns — risk or inefficiency?

pages.title: Definitions
pages.summary: No uniform definition: profitable, safe, good governance/growth, high payout, creditworthy, well managed, accounting quality. Buying quality without paying premium prices IS value investing. Two questions: standalone premium? or value enhancer?

pages.title: Quality should matter
pages.summary: Obvious to Graham and the street, resisted by academics; interest rose with the dot-com bust. Central question: how to measure it. Plan: profitability → measure zoo → safety (BAB) → synthesis (QMJ).

pages.title: Novy-Marx: the measure
pages.summary: Gross profitability = (revenues − COGS)/assets. Quality-value link: 'wonderful business at a fair price' (Buffett). Dissimilar holdings: quality is short value, value short quality — each does well when the other bleeds: a natural hedge.

pages.title: The economic argument
pages.summary: Productive assets should out-earn unproductive ones at the same price — same logic as value pointed at the asset side; consistent with risk AND behavioral stories. GP/A predicts returns ESPECIALLY controlling for B/M; explains ROE, market power, default risk, net issuance, organizational capital anomalies.

pages.title: Sorts (Table 2)
pages.summary: GP/A high−low spread 0.31%/mo (t 2.49); FF3 alpha 0.52%/mo (t 4.49). High-GP/A firms are growth-like (negative HML loading) — the alpha exceeds the raw spread.

pages.title: Fama–MacBeth
pages.summary: GP/A slope 0.75 (t 5.49); industry-demeaned 1.00 (t 8.99); survives earnings/FCF/B/M/size/momentum controls.

pages.title: Double sorts
pages.summary: 25 GP/A×B/M portfolios: conditional profitability spread 58bp/mo vs 31 unconditional; conditional value spread 68 vs 41. Each hides the other in raw data.

pages.title: Joint strategies
pages.summary: 50/50 value+profitability roughly doubles the Sharpe of either leg (0.65–0.78 vs market 0.41); shallower drawdowns; survives trading costs.

pages.title: Value insurance
pages.summary: Trailing 5-yr Sharpes strongly negatively related — profitability's best runs (late 1990s) are value's worst.

pages.title: Cumulative joint performance
pages.summary: Combined strategy compounds above components, 1963–2012.

pages.title: International
pages.summary: Profitability spreads positive and significant globally with the same growth-like tilt; combination diversifies globally.

pages.title: Explaining anomalies
pages.summary: Adding a PMU factor drives out alphas of ROE, market power, default-risk, net-issuance, organizational-capital strategies.

pages.title: NM conclusions
pages.summary: Powerful predictor obscured by negative correlation with B/M; challenges rational value stories; explains many strategies.

pages.title: Other quality measures
pages.summary: Graham's 7 criteria (size, current ratio>2, 10yr positive earnings, 20yr dividends, EPS growth ≥1/3, P/E≤15, P/B≤1.5); Grantham; Greenblatt magic formula (ROIC + EBIT/EV); Sloan accruals; Piotroski F-score; defensive (low beta/vol); Novy-Marx profitability.

pages.title: Which survive? (NM 2014)
pages.summary: All measures have some power (small caps, with value) — but only gross profitability earns significant standalone returns and subsumes most of the others.

pages.title: Quality strategies table
pages.summary: Only GP (and marginally ROIC/F-score) earn positive raw returns; alphas larger since quality tilts against value; defensive strategies have MKT loading −0.66 (t −20.4).

pages.title: Spanning tests
pages.summary: GP alpha survives every specification (2.34–4.62%/yr); others largely spanned by GP + value. Carry one signal: profitability.

pages.title: BAB motivation
pages.summary: 1969: Fischer Black at Wells Fargo finds low-beta stocks return too much vs CAPM; Wells Fargo refuses to trade it. FP: theory of funding constraints; global evidence; embedded leverage.

pages.title: Theory: leverage constraints
pages.summary: Constrained investors can't lever the tangency portfolio, so they overweight high-beta assets; market M sits right of tangency T.

pages.title: Proposition 1
pages.summary: E[r] = rf + ψ + β·λ with λ = E[rM]−rf−ψ; ψ = tightness of funding constraints. SML intercept too high, slope too flat: low-beta underpriced, high-beta overpriced. CAPM-alpha = ψ(1−β).

pages.title: Flat SML: stocks
pages.summary: BJS 1972 (1931–65) and updated 1926–2010: realized returns rise far less steeply with beta than CAPM requires.

pages.title: Flat SML: bonds
pages.summary: Beta-sorted bond portfolios 1952–2010 — same picture.

pages.title: Global grid
pages.summary: Alphas decline in beta across US/intl stocks, Treasuries, credit, indices, country bonds, FX, commodities (1964–2009).

pages.title: BAB Sharpe ratios
pages.summary: US stocks BAB Sharpe 0.75 vs HML 0.39, UMD 0.50, SMB 0.25; positive in every country/asset class.

pages.title: Embedded leverage
pages.summary: FM regressions: embedded-leverage coefficient negative and highly significant for equity options, index options, leveraged ETFs — constrained investors pay for built-in leverage.

pages.title: Proposition 3 (TED)
pages.summary: BAB returns fall when funding tightens (rising TED spread); underpricing reasserts when constraints ease.

pages.title: Proposition 5 (holders)
pages.summary: Mutual funds and individuals (leverage-averse) hold high-beta portfolios; LBOs and Berkshire buy low-beta and apply leverage. MPT's identical-portfolio prediction rejected in the BAB direction.

pages.title: QMJ motivation
pages.summary: Cochrane's challenge: explain PRICES, not just returns. Graham–Dodd view vs efficiency view (quality priced fully, normal returns).

pages.title: Five findings
pages.summary: Quality measurable ex ante (persistent ~10yrs); higher prices but LOW R²; QMJ 4F alphas 66bp/mo t=10.2 US, 45bp t=5.5 global; quality looks SAFER, gains in distress; price of quality varies — low price predicts high QMJ returns.

pages.title: Defining quality
pages.summary: Gordon rewrite: P/B = profitability × payout / (required return − growth) — four components: Profitability, Growth, Safety, Payout. Quality = z(Prof + Growth + Safety + Payout) from rank z-scores.

pages.title: Data
pages.summary: Long sample US 1956–2012; Broad sample 24 countries 1986–2012.

pages.title: Price of quality
pages.summary: FM of price z-score on quality: coefficient positive, highly significant — but avg R² only 0.05–0.31.

pages.title: Why low R²?
pages.summary: Three hypotheses: (a) market uses better measures ⟹ our measures shouldn't predict returns; (b) quality is risky ⟹ quality stocks should be risky; (c) underreaction ⟹ quality predicts returns. Test with returns.

pages.title: Quality-sorted portfolios (US)
pages.summary: Returns/alphas rise nearly monotonically; H−L 0.47%/mo (t 2.80); 4F alpha 0.97 (t 8.55); H−L beta −0.38 — quality hedges.

pages.title: Broad sample
pages.summary: Same globally: 4F alpha 0.93 (t 6.06).

pages.title: QMJ factor
pages.summary: QMJ 4F alpha 0.66%/mo (t 10.2) US with NEGATIVE MKT/SMB/HML loadings — safe, big, growing stocks earning high returns troubles any theory of size and value.

pages.title: IRs by country
pages.summary: QMJ information ratios positive in all countries but one.

pages.title: Flight to quality
pages.summary: QMJ vs market: negative and convex — best QMJ returns in sharp declines. Opposite of a risk premium.

pages.title: Analysts
pages.summary: Target prices higher for quality but vary LESS than actual prices ⟹ implied E[r] decreasing in quality; realized returns RISE — underreaction (hypothesis c).

pages.title: Graham–Dodd vs efficiency
pages.summary: (a) fails: quality predicts returns. (b) fails: quality looks safer, gains in distress. (c) consistent with everything. Challenges efficiency (joint hypothesis caveat).

pages.title: QMJ conclusions
pages.summary: QMJ as RHS variable: resurrects the size effect; helps explain Buffett and private equity.

pages.title: Decomposing Buffett
pages.summary: Frazzini–Kabiller–Pedersen: split Berkshire into public (13F) and private (inferred) parts; leverage L = (TA−Cash)/Equity.

pages.title: Buffett's exposures
pages.summary: 6-factor regression: positive MKT/HML, negative SMB; BAB 0.29 (t 2.67), QMJ 0.43 (t 2.34); alpha falls 12.1% (t 3.19) → 6.3% (t 1.58), insignificant.

pages.title: Systematic Buffett
pages.summary: Leveraged cheap-safe-quality portfolio tracks Berkshire's public book.

pages.title: Where this leaves us
pages.summary: Profitability hedges value and subsumes rivals; BAB from leverage constraints, tied to funding; QMJ earns alpha with negative risk loadings and flight-to-quality. Together: recover size, explain anomalies, decompose Buffett. Lean: constraints + behavior — Graham–Dodd formalized.
